## Quick start

Enable checkout for pro tenants and read typed settings through one request scope. Every typed read takes an explicit fallback:

```go
{{QUICKSTART}}
```

Change the theme in the same process. New decisions adopt the update; a captured request keeps its original revision:

```go
{{QUICKSTART_REFRESH}}
```

Application services use `Features` and `Scope`. Keep the native engine at startup for `Refresh`, `Run`, and `Status`. `Features.Snapshot` retains observer and tracking configuration; SDK drivers without genuine snapshots return `ErrUnsupported`.

Use a file or HTTP source with the same engine to load external definitions. Refresh explicitly or run a caller-owned polling loop. The [refresh](examples/refresh/main.go) and [polling](examples/polling/main.go) examples show both workflows.

The root package requires Go 1.24 or newer and has no external runtime dependencies. The complete example catalog includes optional SDK drivers and uses Go 1.26 or newer. Install the root module:

```sh
go get github.com/goforj/feature@{{VERSION}}
```

Optional SDK modules are independently versioned:

```sh
go get github.com/goforj/feature/driver/launchdarklyfeature@{{VERSION}}
go get github.com/goforj/feature/driver/openfeaturefeature@{{VERSION}}
```

Clone and run the complete example:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/goforj/feature.git
cd feature
go -C examples run ./quickstart
```

## Available sources

Native sources are included in the root module:

| Source | Scope | Updates |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MemorySource | One process, no persistence | Replace the document, then refresh clients. |
| FileSource | A regular local JSON file or symlink | Read the path on refresh, including atomic file replacement. |
| HTTPSource | An explicit HTTP endpoint | Bounded complete-document retrieval with caller-owned refresh. |
| SourceFunc | Storage services or another configuration model | Application-owned complete-document retrieval and conversion. |

Source configuration is explicit. The library does not read or modify `.env`, start a global client, or require a flag-management service. See the [versioned JSON contract](docs/contract.md) for targeting rules, limits, failure behavior, and multi-process consistency.

## SDK drivers

The optional adapters keep vendor dependencies and Go requirements outside the root module:

| Driver | Constructors | Minimum Go | Verification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [LaunchDarkly](driver/launchdarklyfeature) | New borrows an SDK client; Open owns initialization and shutdown. | 1.25 | Official Relay Docker container, streaming, analytics forwarding, authentication, and outage recovery. |
| [OpenFeature](driver/openfeaturefeature) | New borrows a client; Open owns an isolated API and provider. | 1.26 | GO Feature Flag Docker service in remote and in-process modes; LaunchDarkly provider through its official Relay container. |

Every runtime module requires exact 100% unit statement coverage. The separate [integration suite](integration) checks real services and SDK transports with race detection; its [execution report](docs/integration-results.json) identifies tested versions and source. See the [capability matrix](docs/capabilities.md) for value types, integer precision, provider differences, and current implementation boundaries. Hosted LaunchDarkly account verification remains pending. Features is the portable application API; native Client retains source refresh and genuine snapshots.

## Runnable examples

Run from the repository root:

```sh
go -C examples run ./quickstart   # Typed flags, tenant targeting, live updates, and snapshots.
go -C examples run ./portable     # Portable checks and typed request targeting.
go -C examples run ./typed        # Typed flags, application structs, arrays, and fallbacks.
go -C examples run ./validation   # Definition paths and safe authoring diagnostics.
go -C examples run ./rules        # Typed targeting, variants, weighted splits, and timed rollouts.
go -C examples run ./events       # Observability, tracking, and change subscriptions.
go -C examples run ./http         # HTTP configuration and webhook delivery.
go -C examples run ./native-provider # Native engine through an ordinary OpenFeature SDK.
go -C examples run ./targeting    # Attributes and stable percentage rollout.
go -C examples run ./refresh      # File replacement and request snapshots.
go -C examples run ./polling      # Owned, cancellable refresh loop.
go -C examples run ./launchdarkly # Borrowed and owned SDK adapters, offline data.
go -C examples run ./openfeature  # Borrowed and owned SDKs, memory provider.
```

Tests execute every listed program and verify its output. [Browse the complete examples](examples), including [application structs and arrays](examples/typed/main.go), [definition validation](examples/validation/main.go), [variants, splits, and timed rollouts](examples/rules/main.go), and the [quick start](examples/quickstart/main.go).

The [portable example](examples/portable/main.go) shows the application-facing Features API. Native Client retains explicit source refresh and snapshot operations; Features borrows any Evaluator and provides short checks and owned targeting scopes.

## How it works

- **Local decisions:** the native evaluator reads local snapshots. Optional observers and SDK providers follow their configured I/O policy. Rules match in order; otherwise the configured default applies.
- **Explicit fallback:** missing flags, invalid inputs, or canceled evaluations use the caller's fallback. Evaluate explains the result.
- **Complete publication:** refresh validates a full document before publishing one immutable revision.
- **Failure retention:** refresh failures retain the previous revision. Initial load failures prevent construction.
- **Process boundaries:** each process refreshes independently. Shared documents provide eventual convergence, with no fleet-wide atomic switch.

## Development

```sh
make test-unit       # Execute tests and examples; require exact library coverage.
make test-race       # Include race instrumentation in executable examples.
make test-integration # Require Docker; test real services and SDK transports.
make vet
make record-unit     # Refresh tracked evidence after relevant source changes.
make generate
make check-generated
```

See [development](docs/development.md) for module ownership, validation commands, and publication status. Framework integration, hosted providers, and administration interfaces are separate from this standalone library.

The [remaining-work checklist](docs/roadmap.md) tracks library review, real-App validation, GoForj integration, and release preparation. The [provider study](docs/provider-study.md) records the design research; both initial SDK adapters and their local service integration suites are implemented.
